summary: Block 5: audited the exact paper application of FiveCycleResidues and found the pairing ill-typed - RETRACTED. The five-cycle data live on two copies of Z/5Z: vertex labels k (with D_i={i,i+2}) and state indices i (with S(a), P_j={j-1,j+2}, {0,1}, {2,4}). The correct compatible pair is g(k)=3-k and h(i)=1-i, tied by g(D_i)=D(h(i)) (check: {3-i,1-i}={1-i,3-i}). The map I had used, k->1-k, induces the state map i->4-i, which does NOT send P_1 to P_4 - so the old pairing could not support step 5 at all, even though all nine finite statements were true. Fixed: FiveCycleResidues.lean rewritten with both levels, the commuting identity g_induces_h, the guard lemma one_minus_k_induces_four_minus_i, and the per-condition transport written out in the header (V via label_transport, D trivial, N via h(i+1)=h i - 1, anchor and pair24 fixed setwise, P_1 <-> P_4). AUDIT-FIVE-CYCLE.md got a block-5 retraction banner 0b, corrected 4a/4b, and a new 4c. New finite fact: validity at positions 0 AND 1 alone already gives 0 solutions, so the repair needs only (NC-1) - not (V3), not four positions; this corroborates the angular worker's 'two positions suffice' as a finite fact while showing it presupposes (NC-1). FIVE-CYCLE-CORE remains WITHHELD: stronger finite theorem compiling + moser_recheck.log (standard axioms, rc 0) is remote evidence about those artefacts, not an application to §6.3.4. Recorded that the connected-set check needs Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Uniform (ContinuousSub). No Lean built, one <1 s computation.

escalation.obstacle: (NC-1), restated precisely: at an accumulation point x of a specified five-cycle locus, with a = lim h_n/|h_n| and R the rotation acting on directions, the list S(R a) = {i : R a lies in the closed essential support of state i at x} has no common label, i.e. the intersection of the diagonals D_i over i in S(R a) is empty.
escalation.definitions: D_i = {i, i+2} in Z/5Z; state i at x = the set of directions whose palette is exactly D_i; closed essential support S_i = the closed set whose every neighbourhood meets state i in positive measure; S(u) = {i : u in S_i}.
escalation.hypotheses_available: (6.6) a.e. transition rule at x; closedness and finiteness of the five supports; no-common-label at a and -a from the endpoint pair (a_n^+, a_n^-) and 'y_n in H_k for every label'; (D) disjointness of adjacent position lists; (N) neighbour existence in both directions.
escalation.attempted: direct transport of the printed zero-area endpoint argument (needs a partner direction whose sum lies near a centre with all five edges present; none exists at r=1); derivation from V0,V3,D,N (fails: 8 countermodels, all relaxing 1,2,4,5); single-position weakening (fails: one relaxation never gives a model).
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a proof of (NC-1) — then FIVE-CYCLE-CORE's five-step elimination of Lemma 6.7 stands as a real simplification — or a construction of an accumulation configuration realising S(1) = {2,4}, which would prove Lemma 6.7 is not removable by support-list combinatorics alone.
